title_yt: What If You Got Paid Every Second Like GTA 5? #Shorts
title_fb: What if you got paid what GTA 5 sold, every second?
hook: What if you got paid G, T, A five's sales every second?
open_loop: Hook plants 'how much per second?' (bubble at ~3 s). Per-second amount at line 3, then new numbers each beat (car, per day). The held reveal is the one-second-a-day-for-a-year total ($1.4M) in line 6, which sets up the A/B in line 7.
payoff: One second of GTA 5's estimated sales (~$3,858) paid once a day for a year is about $1.4 million.

lines.text: What if you got paid *G, *T, *A *5's sales every second?
lines.say: What if you got paid G, T, A five's sales every second?
lines.visual: Frame 0: Benny (money outfit) in lemonade apron at his tiny stand, smug, holding a cup; a giant generic cash register is already in frame on the right with a gold '$ / SECOND' counter at $0 and a wall clock. Plain white outlined text 'GTA 5' (no logo). Bubble 'HOW MUCH?!' on 'every second' plants the question.

lines.text: It sold *about *one *billion dollars in three days.
lines.say: It sold about one billion dollars in three days.
lines.visual: Badge 'ESTIMATED SALES'; stamp '3 DAYS'; counter climbs to $1 BILLION; Benny gasps, hops, cup drops. Cash rains from the register.

lines.text: That pays you *almost *four thousand dollars every second.
lines.say: That pays you almost four thousand dollars every second.
lines.visual: Tick sfx each second; each tick the register fires a cash stack and a '+$3,858' badge; cash piles up and buries Benny to his head, only his eyes and a coin on his head visible; thud sfx. Gold counter $3,858 with 'ABOUT'.

lines.text: You buy a *ten-thousand-dollar car in *three seconds.
lines.say: You buy a ten-thousand-dollar car in three seconds.
lines.visual: Benny digs out, hero pose, a generic cartoon car prop-style sketch (plain, no brand) slides in; badge 'EXAMPLE: $10,000 CAR'; clock ticks 1-2-3 with ding. Benny flexes, happy.

lines.text: By tomorrow, you would have *about *three *hundred *thirty *million dollars.
lines.say: By tomorrow, you would have about three hundred thirty million dollars.
lines.visual: Stamp 'QUIT' slams on the lemonade stand; Benny throws his apron and flips a coin, shades-on smug; the hooded stranger (friend) runs in, begs with bubble 'LOAN?!', Benny shrugs. Counter to $333,000,000 'ABOUT PER DAY'; coin rain.

lines.text: One second a day is about *one *point *four million a year.
lines.say: One second a day is about one point four million a year.
lines.visual: Calendar flips with 365 pages flying; each page drops a '$3,858'; counter climbs to $1.4 MILLION; confetti; Benny shocked then happy. Small badge 'NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE'.

lines.text: Would you take that, or *one million now? Comment *A or *B.
lines.say: Would you take that, or one million now? Comment A or B.
lines.visual: Benny points at viewer, thinking; list rows 'A: 1 SECOND A DAY' and 'B: $1 MILLION NOW'; stranger shrugs. Gold headline 'COMMENT A OR B'. Hard cut after the last word (tail ~0.3 s).

facts_used.claim: GTA 5 sold over $1 billion in its first 3 days (retail sales estimate).

math_check: Python: $1e9 / 3 = $333,333,333 per day ('about three hundred thirty million'); / 86,400 = $3,858.02 per second ('almost four thousand', exact $3,858 on screen); $10,000 car / 3,858 = 2.59 s -> 'three seconds' (hypothetical car, labelled EXAMPLE); $3,858.02 x 365 = $1,408,177 -> 'about one point four million'. Revenue (sales), not profit: wording says 'sold' / 'sales'. A/B: one second of pay a day for a year (~$1.4M, paid daily) vs $1M now is a pay-over-time vs lump-sum choice; A is larger in total, so the dilemma is patience vs certainty.
word_count_note: Counted on 'say' (G, T, A five = 4 words).
ip_notes: 'GTA 5' is plain topic text only. No Rockstar characters, logos, lettering, footage, art or music; register and car are generic cartoon props.

upload.title: What If You Got Paid Every Second Like GTA 5?
upload.description:
What would you do with the money GTA 5 sold every single second? 💰
Would you take one second of that pay every day for a year, or $1 million now? Comment A or B!
By sales estimates, GTA 5 sold over $1 billion in its first 3 days. That is about $3,858 every second, and about $1.4 million if you got just one second a day for a year.
Not financial advice. Estimated retail sales (not profit). Source: Engadget, Shacknews.

changes_from_previous: (1) Viewer is now the earner: hook 'What if you got paid G, T, A five's sales every second?' and Benny gets the cash (buried in it, buys a car, quits lemonade, friend begs). (2) Bait-and-switch removed; 'earned/made' replaced by 'sold/sales', 'over/about' hedges and ESTIMATED SALES badge. (3) New number each beat: $1B/3 days, almost $4,000/s, $10,000 car in 3 s (labelled hypothetical), about $333M by tomorrow, about $1.4M for one second a day for a year; no repeated rate, cups dropped. (4) Exact $3,858 only on screen; speech says 'almost four thousand'. (5) Question 'how much per second?' planted in frame 0 bubble, reveal held to line 6. (6) Register in frame 0; physical gags with consequences (cash burial, apron quit). (7) Clear A/B: one second a day for a year vs one million now. (8) Upload: title curiosity gap without exact number, 'Not financial advice.', tag 'gta 5 sales record' added, loose tags removed.
